questions.question: Which deliverable shapes do you want for the 6 scenarios?

options.label: A) PHPUnit Feature tests (Recommended)
options.description: tests/Feature/Scenarios/*.php using CreditLineScenarioBuilder. Asserts numbers, runs in CI.

options.label: B) Dusk browser tests
options.description: tests/Browser/Scenarios/*.php — drives the UI, screenshots. Must run in main `familyfund` container (pool slots lack ChromeDriver). Highest value for S1, S2, S5.

options.label: C) Seeder + artisan command
options.description: db:seed --class=ComplexScenariosSeeder so a human can lease a preview env and click through. Pairs naturally with the UI review I'll do afterward.

questions.question: Want me to lease a preview env and walk through every scenario in a real browser after writing them?

options.label: Yes — full UI review per scenario (Recommended)
options.description: Per the UI-verify memory rule: lease a pool env, seed the scenarios, drive each in browser (covering error/empty/role/mobile where relevant), share URLs + screenshots.

options.label: Yes — UI review only for S1, S2, S5
options.description: Skip browser walkthrough for S3/S4/S6 (those are mostly invariants better proved in PHPUnit).

options.label: No browser review — tests only
options.description: Skip the lease + browser step. Faster, but I'll explicitly say UI wasn't visually verified.

questions.question: How should this work be sequenced?

options.label: Land scenarios first, rename later (Recommended)
options.description: Write the 6 scenarios using current `credit_line` names so they're in CI immediately; do the rename in a follow-up PR.

options.label: Rename first, then scenarios
options.description: Big rename lands first; scenarios use new names from day one. Slower start; larger blast radius.

options.label: One PR for everything
options.description: Bundle rename + scenarios. Big diff but no in-between state.

I'll explore the codebase to understand the existing borrowing/payment/goal/credit-line domain before designing the scenarios. Let me kick off targeted exploration in parallel.

I have the domain map. Now let me also inspect the shares/balances table shape (since the credit-line acts as a balance reduction, not new credit) and check goal/borrowing interactions before proposing scenarios.

Now I have what I need. Before writing scenarios, here are the findings on shape + naming, and a proposal — I want your call on direction before generating code.

## Shape of the shares (balances) table

`account_balances` (one row per (account, type, period)):
| col | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | bigint PK | |
| `type` | `string(3)` | `OWN` \| `BOR` (no enum constraint — string) |
| `shares` | `decimal(19,4)` | |
| `account_id` | FK accounts | |
| `transaction_id` | FK transactions | triggering txn |
| `previous_balance_id` | FK self | temporal chain |
| `start_dt`, `end_dt` | dates | `end_dt=9999-12-31` = active row |

Load-bearing invariants:
- **Exactly one `BOR` row per account per time period.** It holds Σ `outstanding_shares` across all **active** lines.
- Per-line breakdown is reconstructed from `transactions` filtered by `account_credit_line_id` (BOR − REP).
- Net = `OWN − BOR` (`AccountExt::sharesAsOf` `app1/family-fund-app/app/Models/AccountExt.php:123-128`).
- Per-line temporal history lives in a **separate** mirror table `account_credit_line_balances` (5/13 migration) — same shape, scoped to one line.

So your statement is structurally correct: a draw doesn't add new "credit" anywhere — it raises `BOR` so net falls. `OWN` is untouched.

## Naming — should we rename?

"Credit line" misleads in three ways: (1) implies new spendable money, (2) implies revolving, (3) hides the fact that the math is purely a balance offset against `OWN`. Candidates:

- **Share Advance** *(my pick)* — fits the math: beneficiary draws shares forward against their own balance, repays later. Honest about "no new money."
- **Share Loan** / **Beneficiary Loan** — neutral and accurate.
- **Encumbrance** — technically right (lien on own shares) but jargon.
- **Pledge** — wrong direction.

If you agree, the rename is mechanical but wide: tables (`account_credit_lines`, `credit_line_payments`, `credit_line_payment_allocations`, `credit_line_adjustments`, `account_credit_line_balances`), columns (`account_credit_line_id`, `credit_line_match_status`), services (`CreditLine\*`), routes, views, Livewire components, tests. Worth doing in one dedicated PR — out of scope for the scenario task itself.

## Proposed scenarios (for automation)

Six scenarios, each a deterministic builder so the same setup feeds PHPUnit assertions **and** the browser walkthrough:

- **S1 — Multiple draws, one paid off, no interference.** Beneficiary with 2 lines (different terms/frequencies), L1 fully repaid → `paid_off`, BOR drops to L2's outstanding only.
- **S2 — REP routing matrix.** Same beneficiary, 2 lines w/ equal scheduled rows → exact-share REP = `ambiguous` → manual split → `manual`. Then payoff-by-outstanding REP → `auto_matched` via priority-3. Plus a REP on a line-less account → `unmatched`. Asserts `OutstandingCalculator` correctly **ignores** `ambiguous`/`unmatched`/`reversed`.
- **S3 — Non-interaction with PUR/SAL/MAT.** Beneficiary borrows; then a fund **matching** rule fires on a deposit (MAT txn), then a PUR, then a SAL. Assert BOR/outstanding/allocations untouched (proves the matcher's REP-only guard at `CreditLineMatcher.php:48-52`).
- **S4 — Backdated draw + late sweep.** Origination 6 mo ago; `LateDetector::detectAll()` marks past-due rows `late`; a single catch-up REP lands on oldest row → `paid`, rest stay `late`.
- **S5 — Goals react to borrowing.** Goal target=1000; draw 200 drops goal "Current" from 500→300 (net = OWN−BOR per memory rule); repay restores it. Adds a second goal using `target_pct` to confirm both flavors track net.
- **S6 — Readjustment + reversed REP.** Open, 2 REPs, readjust 12→18 mo (new `CreditLineAdjustment`, old rows `cancelled`, fresh schedule), then reverse one REP — outstanding restored, allocation preserved as audit but excluded by `reversed=true` filter.

## Deliverable shape — need your call

The same scenarios can ship in three forms; I'd recommend **A + C**, with **B** following for the highest-value scenarios:
